chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Faddal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or someone who asked him was informed about a man who visits his wife in that place (the private chamber) while in the house there is a group (of people). He said to me and raised his voice: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever imposes on his slave/male servant what he cannot bear, let him sell him.'
Then he looked at the faces of the people in the house, then leaned towards me and said: 'There is no harm in it (i.e., it is permissible).'.

key_terms.فِي ذَلِكَ الْمَوْضِعِ: in that place (referring to the private chamber/bedroom)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it
key_terms.يَأْتِي الْمَرْأَةَ: visits the wife (referring to sexual intercourse)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a husband to have intercourse with his wife while others are in the house?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of marital intimacy in the presence of others, a topic of juristic debate regarding the degree of privacy required. He initially cites the prophetic tradition regarding freeing a slave from undue burden (*man kallafa...*) as a preliminary analogy for removing hardship, but upon observing the listeners' reactions, he explicitly permits it (*la ba'sa bihi*), indicating that the presence of others does not invalidate the act provided modesty is maintained. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on flexibility in private matters (*khawass*) while balancing social decorum.
